newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Active Australian stocks end higher, eye wages.
newsitem.headline: Active Australian stocks end higher, eye wages.

text.p: An interest rate focussed Australian share market ended stronger but off its highs on Wednesday with hopes for another rate cut rising after key local inflation data came in on market expectations.
The All Ordinaries index jumped 27.0 to 2,683.4 after touching an intraday high of 2,696 shortly after the release of the second quarter inflation data.
Traders took a positive lead early from Wall Street's relentless run, saying rate pressures in the U.S. had eased.

"Wall Street had a big run last night with Greenspan's comments that the economy was in good shape and that there was no need for immediate action on interest rates," said Hartley Poynton broker, Robin Forbes, adding the upbeat tone there had combined with local interest rate hopes to help the market head higher.
"On the local scene we have followed that plus the very low inflation figures. If the wages figures out tomorrow are on the low side then everyone will be expecting another rate cut."
May quarter wages data is due at 0130 GMT on Thursday.

The banking sector stormed ahead, highlighting the focus on interest rates. Commonwealth Bank led the way, touching a record high of A$17.00 (US$12.58) early before easing to close 50 cents higher, buoyed by a broker's report that again raised the possibility of a capital return rather than a share buyback.

ANZ Bank and Westpac Banking Corp also hit record highs before retreating to each close over two percent higher. ANZ peaked at A$10.39 before ending at A$10.36, while Westpac topped out at A$8.20 before closing at A$8.16. Sector heavyweight National Bank climbed over one percent to end at A$19.50.
Macquarie Bank shares kept their uptrend, adding 1.1 percent to A$13.20 after predicting better first quarter earnings.
The major miners BHP, Rio Tinto and WMC all ran into profit-takers in the afternoon, the pressure of soft metals prices proving too much and slashing prices from early highs.
BHP ended just four cents higher at A$17.98 after touching an intraday high of A$18.35.

"Nickel and copper prices have really been soft over the last week or so and gold has just added to the (weak) sentiment," said Hartley Poynton's Forbes, a sentiment echoed by other market participants.
"The miners didn't have as many reasons to run and that told in the end," said a dealer at a Sydney-based investment house.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about nine to five, while about 27 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
